v11.80 - b-13: adaptif misyon köprüden sürülebiliyor, iki okumanın tavanı var

The ops were all there and no second `objectives.*` namespace was ever opened.
What was missing was what they SAID, and two of them answered without a ceiling.

WHAT A CALLER COULD NOT READ BACK

  · `missions.list` had no `mode`. So every adaptive-only field elsewhere was an
    absence with two possible meanings — not adaptive, or adaptive and nothing
    recorded yet. It also returned `agent: "d:/zone/agent/ajanlar/asistan"` where
    a name belongs (X-85's lesson, one surface further out).
  · `missions.status` could not say the strategy IN FORCE, whether a steer had
    actually been delivered, whether the journal was sound, or what the run had
    started and not finished. Those are the four questions "what is it doing?"
    decomposes into.
  · a step said it had run a workflow or a nested mission and handed back no id
    to follow it with.

Now: `mode` · `project` · `phase` · `strategyVersion` · criterion, evaluation,
conversation, council and message counts · `pending` {question, approval,
guidance} · `trace` {journalled, degraded} on every LIST row; and on `status`
`strategy`, `guidance` with a real delivery state (pending | inflight | applied
— two-phase delivery has three states and `missions.guide` could only ever
promise the first), `trace` {health, resume, degraded, snapshotBehind} from the
SAME reconciler the reload uses, `frontier` (started and not finished), plus
`taskId`/`workflowRunId`/`missionRunId`/`sessionId`/`outputFile` per step.

THE CEILINGS

`missions.list` returned every run the farm has ever made; `missions.conversation`
every message of a conversation, each one's body read off disk through the
speaker's engine. Both page now, through ONE shared contract — `bridgePage` in
core/bridge.ts, which the whole bridge can use rather than each op inventing its
own. KEYSET, not offset: these lists grow at the END while a caller reads them,
so an offset re-reads or skips a row every time one arrives. An unknown cursor is
REFUSED — silently re-serving page one is indistinguishable from an honest answer
to the caller who then reads the newest rows twice. `more` is computed from the
position, never from `rows.length === limit`, which is wrong exactly when the
last page is full.

`missions.trace` reads the journal FORWARDS (it returned the LAST n events — the
wrong end of an audit record) with `after` as a seq and `kinds` as a filter
applied BEFORE the page is cut, so a limit of 50 gives 50 MATCHING events rather
than the matches inside the first 50. A misspelled kind matches nothing and is
named back in `unknownKinds`; falling back to "no filter" would answer a typo
with the whole journal. The kind vocabulary is one runtime list and the TYPE is
derived from it, so the catalog can print it and can never be one kind behind.

ONE READ OF THE JOURNAL

`missions.status` needs the journal for two of the fields above, and a status
call is what an agent POLLS with — a JSONL re-parse per poll for the life of a
run is the cost curve X-126/X-127 already put this farm through. There were
three independent `reconcileRun` sites (reload, missions.trace, the page's trace
view) and the page kept its own cache keyed on the SNAPSHOT's `lastSeq`. That key
is not the file: the journal is appended first and the snapshot saved second, so
between the two the file holds events `lastSeq` has not counted, and a repaint in
that window drew a graph missing the work that had just started. One memo now,
keyed on size + mtime, shared by all three reading surfaces; the reload still
reconciles directly, before there is any memo to trust.

AND WHAT THIS LAYER IS NOT, said in the catalog so an agent stops looking for it:
there is NO cost optimisation in a mission. No cheap-first routing, no model
escalation, no budget reserve, no expected-value stop. The limits are MECHANICAL
CEILINGS; cost and tokens are recorded as observation and nothing routes on them.
The planner is Claude Code in both modes — not a default, but what the control
flow parses — while delegations run on whichever engine the mission or member
names.

Measured in test/test_mission_bridge_plane.js (new, 53) — including the full
final page, the row inserted before the cursor, the refused cursor, the filter
that must run before the cut, and the typo that must be named — plus
test_mission_reload.js, which now counts two reconcile sites instead of three
and holds the memo to the file rather than the seq. 14042 tests pass.
